newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk conscientious objector jailed for six months.
newsitem.headline: Turk conscientious objector jailed for six months.

text.p: A Turkish military court on Tuesday sent a 26-year-old peace protester to six months in jail for refusing to do national service, Anatolian news agency said.
It said the court found protester Osman Murat Ulke guilty of breaking two laws which forbid statements "aiming to break national strength and alienate the public from the military".

Ulke, head of the banned War Resisters' Association in the western city of Izmir, in 1995 burned his military draft documents publicly and told a news conferance he would refuse to take part in any form of military service,
Turkish laws do not allow any room for conscientious objection to military service, legally compulsory for up to 18 months for every Turkish male from 20 years of age.
Several other members of the association and members of peaceful religious movements have been jailed in the past for refusing to do national service.
The court also ordered that Ulke be sent to a military base to begin military service but he said he would refuse to put on a military uniform.
